dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No formal quarterly guidance (group gives annual guidance only), but H2 26 color from the call: Household expected up low-to-mid single digit; Professional double digit for FY26 with normalization to high single digit in H2 on tougher comps; July trading in line with expectations; nutrition expected flat to improving; comfort sold out in Europe (no further July upside); FX impact marginal at EBITDA level for the year.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 guidance RAISED on the call (30/07/2026): adjusted EBITDA now EUR 670-690M (vs EUR 640-660M previously), revenue growth confirmed at mid-single digit. The raise reflects the immediate EUR 15M benefit from US duty (IEEPA) refunds booked in Q2 and strong Professional momentum, while factoring in expected logistics/materials cost pressure and the current US tariff scenario (~10-12%, seen as neutral); any additional duty refunds would come on top. A&P spend ~EUR 200M expected for the year; no commitment to repeating ~EUR 500M annual FCF but generation expected in line with historical average.
pointsCles: H1 26 beat with high-quality mix: revenue EUR 1,676.3M (+5.8%, +8.0% cc) and adjusted EBITDA EUR 283.7M (16.9% margin vs 15.2%), driven by Professional (La Marzocco/Eversys) at +36.3% (+40% cc) with a 32% divisional margin (~30% ex EUR 4M duty refunds/one-offs) - fourth straight quarter above +30%; Household returned to historical mid-single-digit organic pace in Q2 (+5.1% cc) after early-year destocking.

FY26 guidance raised: adjusted EBITDA now EUR 670-690M (from 640-660M), revenue growth confirmed mid-single digit; the raise embeds the EUR 15M IEEPA duty refunds booked in Q2 (op-cost credit, ~4M Professional / ~11M Household) plus Professional outperformance, and factors in logistics/materials cost pressure and the current ~10-12% US tariff regime (any further refunds would be incremental); H2 color: Household low-to-mid single digit, Professional normalizing to high single digit on tougher comps (double digit FY).

Structural dynamics: espresso premiumization and prosumer growth keep fueling a fragmented, broad-based Professional expansion (new Eversys key accounts in Europe, North America and China; revenue synergies between brands still to come); balance sheet firepower is large (net cash EUR 686.6M, trailing-12M FCF ~EUR 508M) with buying out the ~38% Professional minorities stated as the #1 capital-allocation priority - a potential EPS-accretion catalyst with no timetable.

Risks flagged on the call: MEIA down 12.2% in Q2 on Gulf geopolitics, nutrition/NutriBullet still declining (stabilizing at best), negative price/mix of EUR 15-16M from widening promo windows testing Household pricing power (management calls it temporary), and much tougher Professional comps from H2 26 and into 2027; guidance top end conditional on no geopolitical deterioration.

hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Sum-of-the-parts between a mature/cyclical Household core and a hypergrowth Professional division (La Marzocco, Eversys). H1 2026 exceeded the catch-up trajectory: revenue 1,676.3M (+8.0% cc) against a strong comp, adjusted EBITDA margin 16.9% (vs 15.2%), and the FY26 EBITDA guidance RAISED to 670-690M (from 640-660M). Professional grew +40% cc at a 32% margin; Household rebounded (+4.5% Q2, +5.1% cc) exactly as management promised in April. Net cash 686.6M despite an ongoing buyback (30M of 60M spent).

== THESIS READ ==
- Professional is the thesis engine: +40% cc, 32% S1 margin - management frames ~30% as the normalized mid-term margin and 'low double digit' as the long-term growth rate; mix keeps lifting the group margin. Watch: H2 normalization to 'high-SD' guided growth against stiff comps.
- Household stabilizes low-to-mid SD from H2, with a -15/16M price/mix drag (widened promo windows) seen stabilizing, offset by a 2027 innovation wave (coffee, espresso, nutrition, food prep). Watch: price/mix inflection and Kenwood/nutrition trends.
- Tariffs now roughly neutral: 15M of refunds booked as cost rebates (4M Professional / 11M Household), none further expected. Watch: reclassification risk in H2 margins.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Guidance is on adjusted EBITDA; no per-share consensus tracked (basis null). Minority buyout optionality (La Marzocco) and Professional M&A pipeline (North America preferred) sit on top of a net-cash balance sheet. Capital priorities stated: operations, buybacks, M&A.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
FY26: S1 actual + H2 on reaffirmed mid-SD guidance -> revenue ~4,004M; EBITDA at the raised mid (680M) less D&A run-rate -> EBIT ~525M; ETR 27.5%; finNet ~0 (interest income offset by FX/hedging). 2027-2030: setup growth rates applied to the higher 2026 base. Bridge reconciles published 2025 at ~0 residual. Watch: Professional H2 growth print; marketing envelope ~200M/yr; buyback completion.

== CATALYSTS ==
9M results (Nov); 2027 innovation launches; Professional M&A / minority buyout; buyback completion.

ancrages.moteur: The Household catch-up anticipated at the previous refresh (FY26 guidance reaffirmed despite a Q1 at -2,4%) is confirmed by the actual figures: Q2 26 revenue +8,4% reported (+9,2% cc), bringing H1 growth to +8,0% cc - a performance above the mere normalisation expected, on an H1 2025 comparable that was itself very strong (+11,3%).

Professional confirms its hypergrowth at +40% cc over the full half-year, in line with Q1 (+40,1%) - no sign of a slowdown at this stage despite the markedly tougher H2-26 comparables (H2-25 base >30%) already identified at the previous refresh as a factor of expected mechanical deceleration.

Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised at H1 26 from 640-660 M EUR to 670-690 M EUR (+4,6% at the midpoint) - bottom-up reconstruction adopted: actual H1 26 (adjusted EBITDA 283,7 M EUR, margin 16,9%) + H2 26 estimated by extending the margin expansion observed (Professional mix effect, discipline on operating costs), giving an FY2026 EBIT (Omnium basis, after D&A) revised to ~525 M EUR (vs 491 M EUR at the previous refresh, +6,9%).
US customs tariff impact confirmed sharply lower since Q1 26 (~4M€ net in Q1, against 10-15M€ net in FY25) - no new information contradicting that trajectory in H1, assumption unchanged.

The growing weight of Professional in group revenue is pulling the group margin up - confirmed and even amplified by the margin expansion observed in H1 26 (+170bp on adjusted EBITDA H1 vs H1 25), beyond the simple +15bp/yr assumption adopted at the previous refresh.

Buyout of the La Marzocco/Eversys minorities (~38% minority interests) still the no. 1 capital allocation priority per the creation thesis - no announcement identified in the sources consulted for this H1 26 refresh, not modelled.

Net financial position still solidly positive (686,6 M€ at 30/06/2026, vs 345,8 M€ a year earlier) despite the normal seasonal decline vs end-2025 (770 M€, tied to the dividend payment) - M&A/buyback optionality confirmed and even strengthened.

historique.message: EBITDA guidance raised to 670-690M on Professional strength (S1 +36%, +40% cc; EBITDA margin 32% vs 26.4% - management frames ~30% as the normalized mid-term level and 'low double digit' as long-term growth) and 15M of tariff refunds booked as cost rebates (4M Professional / 11M Household, none further expected). Household rebounded as promised (+4.5% Q2; Americas +20.8% cc on espresso machines) with a -15/16M price/mix drag from widened promo windows, seen stabilizing. July trading 'in line'. Capital priorities: operations, then buybacks (30/60M spent), then Professional M&A, North America preferred. FCF 12m rolling 508M; net cash 686.6M.
